WS4's 22.8bp is the same STRIPS basis with yields unchanged instead (about $293,000): a different convention, not the buyable ladder. Under the adopted rule reading R1(a) her real ladder is the WInS-listed one; sized to pay exactly $50,000 a rung it costs about $289,200 today, within $100 of STRIPS (`rab/results/M2/bookL_basis_check.txt`), so its room is about the same. Use one basis in the note, the reflection and the IPS; if it fails on Friday: do not stop. Buy orders 1-10 from the `--split-from-curve` ticket (more in the dated holdings, less VT): the IPS says the 2028 deposit completes the earliest payments, so less is left for the facility (friday_checklist.md; exemplar IBTR_F in s5); who absorbs a gap: the 2028 deposit tops up the earliest payments first, so no payment is missed and less is left for the facility. 'The facility gets less' is true on either reading. 'Latest payments first' is the IPS funding rule, not the order of WInS trades; thinnest fund: about $38m in assets (iShares, 28 Sep); place it after the first hour. Sizes: Portfolio #1: 846 shares, expected Preview total $19,897.54 (ticket), 6.6% of the book (numbers.yaml); Laura's plan: about $29,000 of her 2027 deposit buys this rung; if its income is reinvested at only 2%, it delivers about $46,000 of the $50,000 (reinvest.rung.IBTR, MODEL; appendix only, never in a note). On Friday type the words the refresh prints for that day's break-even: under 22.5bp 'about a fifth', 22.5 to 30bp 'about a quarter', 30 to 37.5bp 'about a third' [laura.ladder.breakeven_fall_bp_strips (26.2bp, MODEL, 28 Sep curve, zero-coupon basis, forward convention); Friday's figure is the refresh line, written in the Trade Log and re-locked by WS1 (request 1). $50,000 and $300,000 are case facts].
